newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Svyazinvest would treat Rostelekom as subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Svyazinvest would treat Rostelekom as subsidiary.

text.p: Russia's Svyazinvest telecom holding company will treat international telecom Rostelekom like any other subsidiary if the government transfers control to it, Svyazinvest's general manager said on Thursday.
"It will be under (our) control if the share packet is transferred," Nail Ismailov, general manager of Svyazinvest told Reuters. "They will be in the same relationship as regional companies."
Svyazinvest has controlling share packets in most Russian regional telecoms and, despite some disputes, has legal control over them.
Government officials, including the Minister of Communications, have said Russia will transfer to Svyazinvest its 38 percent stake in Rostelekom, which includes 51 percent of voting shares.
President Boris Yeltsin is soon to sign a decree on the matter, they have said.
The president of Rostelekom, a rich company and darling of the shares market, had been reported as saying Rostelekom management would not be affected by Svyazinvest ownership.
Asked about such comments, Ismailov replied: "They have a development plan which they are already carrying out, and with which we have agreed many issues."
Ismailov has said that Svyazinvest is in need of investment capital.
He said on Tuesday Svyazinvest would not receive investment funds from planned government sales of about 49 percent of Svyazinvest to foreign and domestic portfolio investors.
Asked if Svyazinvest would use Rostelekom as an income source to fund regional telecom projects, Ismailov replied:

"Naturally there are joint projects in which Rostelekom will take financial part. Regional projects -- today we are constructing an intercity station in Adygeya (Northern Caucasus) together with Rostelekom financing."
"So there is nothing terrible about working together... our regional operator in the Black Earth zone is also laying cable together."
